title: Impact of Precipitation Hardening and Dispersion of Tungsten Carbide Particles on the Mechanical Properties of Al-Cu-Mg/WC Composite Subjected to T6 Treatment
content: The utilization of lightweight, high-strength materials has led researchers to develop composite materials including diverse matrices and reinforcements, thereby enhancing their mechanical properties, including aluminum matrix composites [1]. Aluminum and its alloys are especially appropriate for structural applications due to their properties such as low density, high thermal conductivity, elevated specific strength, and corrosion resistance, having a significant application in the aerospace and automotive industries, where their use to reduce weight and consequently fuel consumption is a critical factor [2]. Alloy 2024, an aluminum alloy primarily composed of Al, Cu, and Mg, is significant for its outstanding mechanical qualities, achieved through a heat treatment technique known as T6 [3]. The reinforcement of aluminum matrix composites (AMC) with ceramic particles, such as Al2O3, TiO2, SiC, AlN, TiC, TiB2 and B4C, has attracted great attention due to the low cost associated with these particles, as demonstrated by different research [4]. Despite extensive research on AMCs, there is a lack of studies regarding the application of heavy refractory reinforcements, such as tungsten carbide (WC). Tungsten carbide (WC) is a heavy refractory material with a high melting point (2870 °C), exceptional hardness (2242 HV), reasonable wear and corrosion resistance, and a high Young's modulus (550 GPa). A key obstacle in synthesizing aluminum matrix composites (AMC) through casting is their low wettability and propensity to form agglomerates [5], which impedes the uniform dispersion of reinforcing particles within the matrix. This interaction between the aluminum matrix and the distribution and size of the reinforcing particles is crucial in determining the fundamental properties of the composite material [6]. To avoid these limitations, powder metallurgy has emerged as an important process, adopted for the preparation of metal matrix composites [7]. Previous studies have shown that an Al-Cu-Mg/WC composite can be synthesized by powder metallurgy, despite the differences in density (15.63 vs. 2.70 g/cm3) and melting points (2870 vs. 660 °C) of the WC and the aluminum alloy, respectively. It should be noted that these characteristics could not have been achieved by conventional methods [8]. A previous literature study focused on the hardness and wear resistance of WC-incorporated AMCs without heat treatment. However, the influence of WC particle addition and heat treatment on these mechanical properties remains to be elucidated. Therefore, the present study aims to conduct a detailed investigation into the significance of the effect of WC particles and heat treatment on the mechanical properties of WC particle-incorporated AMCs.
